transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. What brings you in to see me?

I guess the main thing is I feel like I’m constantly running on a motor lately. I’ll finish something at school or at home, and then I’m immediately on to the next thing. I just don’t feel like I can shut myself off.
Has this feeling of being constantly 'on the go' been something you've noticed since you were a kid, or is this a new change that started recently?

No, it’s not new. I mean, it feels more noticeable lately, but I was like this as a kid too. My mother used to joke that I “taught the class from my seat” because I was always out of my chair, talking, or jumping in before the teacher finished giving directions. So… yeah, it’s been part of me a long time, not just something that started recently.
Have you been using any stimulants, energy drinks, or other recreational drugs recently?
Not really, no. I mean, I drink coffee like most people, but I’m not using recreational drugs or taking anything like that to keep me going. Energy drinks aren’t really my thing.
Have you noticed any unintentional weight loss, feeling unusually hot or sweaty, a racing heart, or hand tremors recently?

No, I haven’t really noticed anything like that. My weight seems about the same, and I don’t think I’ve been unusually hot or sweaty. No hand tremors that I can tell. My heart can feel like it’s going fast if I’m rushing around, but nothing that stands out as unusual.
Would you say these difficulties with restlessness and staying focused cause real problems for you in more than one area of your life—like both at work or school and at home or in relationships?

Yes. It’s causing problems in more than one place. At work it’s gotten pretty serious—I’ve been put on a corrective plan because of the complaints. And at home, my spouse says the caregiving routines are harder because everyone has to manage my energy on top of everything else.

I’m trying to help, but it feels like I’m damaging trust with my colleagues and with my family.
Have you had any distinct periods lasting several days where you felt unusually elated, euphoric, or needed much less sleep than usual without feeling tired?
No, I don’t think so. I have times where I’m wound up or restless, but not like several days of feeling euphoric or needing almost no sleep and still feeling fine.
Thinking back to before you were about 12 years old, can you recall specific examples of being unusually restless, impulsive, or having trouble paying attention in school or at home?

Yes. I remember that pretty clearly. My mother used to joke that even in elementary school I was “teaching the class from my seat,” because I was always out of my chair, talking, or jumping in before the teacher even finished giving directions.

So, this was there way before I was an adult. It doesn’t feel like something that just started with the recent family changes.
Do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks, lose track of what you're doing, or forget appointments and details in daily life?

I’m not really sure on that one. I mean, I can lose my place sometimes like anyone, but I don’t have a clear pattern or specific examples of forgetting appointments or details that I can point to right now.
Do you often have trouble sustaining your attention on tasks or activities, like reading, meetings, or paperwork, finding your mind wandering even when you're trying to focus?

I’m not sure how to answer that clearly. I don’t have a specific example coming to mind with reading or meetings or paperwork where I can say, yes, that happens all the time. My mind can drift some, but I haven’t really tracked it or noticed a clear pattern.
Do you often make careless mistakes or overlook details when doing schoolwork, work tasks, or other activities that require sustained attention?
I’m not sure. I don’t have a clear example where I’d say I’m often making careless mistakes or missing details. I might miss something now and then, but I haven’t noticed it as a regular pattern.
Do you often find yourself interrupting or finishing other people's sentences, or having trouble waiting your turn in conversations or lines?

Yes, I do. I’ll jump into conversations before people are finished—at work with colleagues or parents, and at home with my spouse or relatives. In my head I’m thinking I’m helping or moving things along, but I end up talking over people or kind of taking charge before they’ve had their say.
